summary: IDS s174_triple is degraded: 67.5% of TCP sessions are one-way (needs both directions), 4.3% of frames exceed IDS 1518-byte MTU and are dropped by NIC, and 2.4% of TCP packets show gaps from capture drops. IDS requires full payload and bidirectional streams for reassembly and signature matching.

findings.root_cause: Feed delivers only one direction for 129 of 191 TCP sessions (67.5% >10% threshold). Most likely SPAN/mirror configured on a single direction, asymmetric routing with single-sided TAP, or packet broker policy/filter forwarding only client->server and not aggregating both sides.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs both directions to reassemble TCP streams, track state, and match request+response signatures. With two-thirds of sessions one-way, stateful detection, exploit verification, and file extraction will fail, causing high false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: IDS profile needs_both_directions=true. Broker must aggregate both directions of each flow into this single IDS feed so sessions are complete.

findings.root_cause: 87 of 2035 frames (4.3%) exceed the IDS 1Gbps port MTU of 1518 bytes, largest observed 8058 bytes. Network/broker is forwarding jumbo frames that the IDS NIC silently drops. Tool needs full payload so broker slicing/trimming is not viable.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS is blind to 4.3% of frames. Dropped jumbo frames often carry large payloads, file transfers, or tunneled traffic - attacker can evade detection by using large frames. IDS also loses coverage for those flows.

recommended_fix.why: Cannot use slice/trim because IDS needs full payload. Must either enable jumbo-frame support end-to-end to IDS (NIC/broker/tool config for 9k MTU) or reduce MTU upstream and ensure broker does not forward frames larger than 1518 to this 1G port.

findings.root_cause: 46 of 1881 TCP packets (2.4%) show gaps/retransmissions indicating missing data in transit. Pattern consistent with SPAN/mirror oversubscription or packet broker buffer drops under burst, not tool overload (tool_overload healthy).
findings.impact_on_tool: Gaps break TCP reassembly and stream reconstruction. IDS will miss signatures that span dropped segments, fail to extract files, and generate incomplete flow logs, reducing detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: SPAN drops packets under load/bursts. Replacing SPAN with physical TAP and lossless broker delivery eliminates capture drops before the IDS.
